title: [finding] `packages/spec/liveness/README.md` "Author warnings" still says warnings are opt-in per `authorWarn` row; since #21092 a `dead` or `live-elsewhere` verdict warns on its own
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site.** The landing site is a shipped prose page that now states the opposite of what the shipped lint does.
- **Reader:** the `domain:spec` seat that takes this card. It edits one section of `packages/spec/liveness/README.md`. No code, no ledger rows.
- **Dedupe:** a semantic issue search, open and closed, for "liveness README author warnings authorWarn opt-in dead live-elsewhere" returned 15 hits. None covers this. The nearest are #19269 (a wrong path in the same section, closed) and #16362 (the ledger half of #16094, closed).

## What is wrong

PR #21092 (`Fixes #16094`, merged as `b616c0a63d`, `@objectstack/lint` minor) changed `shouldWarn` in `packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts`:
- A ledger row now warns when its status is `dead`, `live-elsewhere` or `experimental`, or when it sets `authorWarn: true`.
- A verdict-triggered row shows its `authorHint`, else the verdict's default hint, and never its `note`.

`packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, section "Author warnings — closing the loop (`authorWarn`)", at `origin/main` `b616c0a63d`, still teaches the old model:

| Line | Text | Why it is now false |
|:--|:--|:--|
| ~553 | "warnings are **opt-in per entry**" | `dead` and `live-elsewhere` rows warn without opting in. |
| ~557 | `authorWarn: true` warns "(in addition, any `experimental` entry warns by default …)" | The default set is now `experimental`, `dead` and `live-elsewhere`. |
| ~558 | `authorHint` "falls back to `note`" | That holds only for opted-in and `experimental` rows. A verdict-triggered row falls back to the verdict's default hint. |
| ~561–565 | Rule 1: benign display metadata that is `dead` "must NOT be marked; an author isn't misled by them" | Not marking no longer keeps it silent. Grading a benign display key `dead` now warns every author who sets it. |
| ~572 | "coverage grows by marking more entries `authorWarn`" | Coverage now also grows by grading a row `dead` or `live-elsewhere`. |

**Reach:** the page ships. `@objectstack/spec`'s `package.json` `files` lists `liveness`. The cost lands on the next ledger edit. A maintainer who follows rule 1 and grades a benign display key `dead` "unmarked" ships a warning to every author of that key. Under `--strict`, that warning flips `os lint` and `os validate` to exit 1.

The four keys warned today are a view container's own `name` and `label`, and a permission set's `rowLevelSecurity[].label` and `rowLevelSecurity[].description`. They are the `.changeset/16094-liveness-dead-warns.md` measurement, and they are exactly this case: benign display keys graded `dead`, with no `authorWarn`.

## Done when

The section describes the shipped rule:
- Which statuses warn by default.
- What `authorWarn` still adds, which is the only way a `planned` row warns.
- Which hint each kind of row shows.
- That grading a row `dead` or `live-elsewhere` is itself an author-facing act.

Rule 1 then becomes guidance about the verdict, not about the marker. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` and the liveness gates stay green. This changes no row.

Not in scope: #21127 (a `live` row with `authorWarn` throws the integrity sentinel) and #21096 (an opted-in row prints its `note`). Both are open on their own cards.
